main_issue: Whether Agent D, going vegetarian for a month, can keep taking part in the dinner rota by cooking a vegetarian meal on his night and cooking his own portion separately (before 6.30) on others' nights.

A-B.evidence: B says D's early separate cooking is fine (T14, T21, T23, T26: 'What is the actual problem?'); A keeps objecting that it is not the same shared meal (T22, T27).

A-C.evidence: C first agreed with A that separate cooking defeats the rota (T7, T9), then accepted cooking before 6.30 (T18); A still objects (T27).

A-D.evidence: D keeps proposing that they eat together at the same table (T12, T15, T19); A insists it is not a shared meal (T13, T16, T27).

B-C.evidence: B (T14) and C (T18) both say cooking before 6.30 is fine. C earlier raised concerns (T7, T9).

B-D.evidence: B accepts D's earlier cooking (T14) and defends it to A (T21, T23, T26); D's early-cooking proposal (T10) fits B's kitchen-timing concern (T6).

C-D.evidence: C objected to simultaneous cooking (T9); D offered to cook before 6.30 (T10); C accepted: 'that's fine with me' (T18).
